JUSTICE SUNITA AGARWAL) This is a wholly misconceived appeal filed by a person, named as Amraji Ataji through his power of attorney holder namely Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel claiming to be the owner of Revenue Survey No. 87/1, total area of which was initially 2732 sq. mtrs.

sentences.text:
The statement made in paragraph No. '5' of the writ petition are being reproduced hereinunder for ready reference :-
"That the petitioner and his family members are the owners of land NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined bearing survey No. 87/1 admeasuring 2732 sq.mtrs. situated in the sim of village Chiloda (Naroda), Taluka and District Gandhinagar.

A copies of the old village form No. 7/12,
F-Form and Part Plan and Zonning Certificate of Draft T.P.Scheme No. 243 are annexed herewith and marked as Annexure-A Colly.

It is submitted that the subject land is of ownership and possession of the petitioner and his family members and petitioner having possession of 600 square meters reaming land, after acquisition,
the therefore the petitioner has filed the present petition for protection of rights of share of his possession admeasuring 600 sq.mtrs."
2.

A perusal of the said statement shows that the petitioner would contend that he and his family members are the owners of the land bearing Revenue Survey No. 87/1 admeasuring 2732 sq.mtrs.,
situated in the sim of village Chiloda (Naroda), Taluka and District Gandhinagar.
Alongwith the writ petition, copies of the old Village Form No. 7/12, F-Form etc. have been appended as Annexure-A (colly.).

The contention therein is that the subject land is in the ownership and possession of the petitioner and his family members and the petitioner is having possession of 600 sq.mtrs. of the remaining land after acquisition and hence, filed the writ petition for protection of right of share in his possession admeasuring 600 sq.mtrs..

3. The prayers made in the original writ petition are as under :-
"A) That Your Lordships may be pleased to admit and allow this petition.
B) That your Lordships may be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order and/or direction quashing and setting aside the impugned order passed by the Respondents no.3 dated 14/8/2025 and further be pleased to direct the respondent nos.2 and 3 to consider the objection of the petitioner dated 15/4/2025 before submitting the Draft T.P. Scheme for Preliminary Scheme to the respondent No.1 with respect to Survey no.87/1 admeasuring 600 sq.mtrs, which is remaining land as per the order passed by the Land Acquisition Officer, National Highway Authority dated 13/3/2019.
C) Pending admission hearing and final disposal of this petition, Your NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined Lordships may be pleased to stay the execution, operation and implementation of the order passed by the respondent no. 3 dated 14.08.2025.

sentences.text: 4. In the judgment impugned, the learned single Judge records the contention of the learned counsel for the respondent Corporation that the petitioner had created third party rights and therefore, for the land-in-question now the petitioner is no more an owner.

5. Mr. G.H.Virk, the learned counsel for the respondent Corporation has invited attention of the Court to page No. '123' of the paper book, which is the order passed in the first writ petition filed by the petitioner herein, namely Amraji Ataji, registered as Special Civil Application No. 3693 of 2025.

In the said writ petition, the challenge was to the notice dated 20.02.2025 issued under Section 48A read with Section 68 of the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976, read with Rule 33 of the Rules made thereunder.

sentences.text:
The same learned counsel Mr. A.M.Parekh had represented the petitioner in the said writ petition, which was disposed of with the following observations and directions in paragraph No. '6' of the judgment and order dated 27.03.2025 as under :-
"6. Considered the submissions.

It is noticed that the challenge in this petition is notice dated 20.02.2025 issued under Section 48A read with Section 68 of The Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976 and Rule 33 of The Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Rules, 1979, whereby time has been provided to all stake holders to raise their objections.

sentences.text: It is open for the petitioner to raise his objections, if any, against the draft town planning scheme No.243 Ranasan/Muthiya, Nana Chiloda.
Once the objections are filed, the same shall be considered in accordance with law.
Needless to say, that the objections shall be considered NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined before finalization of preliminary Town Planning Scheme."

6. It may also be noted that the learned counsel for the appellant, namely Mr. A.M.Parekh has admitted that Amraji Ataji had executed a registered sale deed dated 29.12.2023 in the name of one Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel.

From a perusal of the judgment and order dated 27.03.2025, it seems that the factum of execution of the sale deed by Amraji Ataji had also not been disclosed in the first round of litigation initiated by him namely Special Civil Application No. 3693 of 2025, and the counsel for the respondent therein had agitated the said issue touching upon the entertainability of the said writ petition, which has led to the issuance the above noted directions.

7. The second writ petition had been filed by Amraji Ataji through his power of attorney holder Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel challenging the order dated 14.08.2025 passed pursuant to the directions issued by this Court in the judgment and order dated 27.03.2025.

It is important to note that even in the second writ petition, out of which the present appeal has arisen, the factum of execution of the sale deed dated 29.12.2023 by Amraji Ataji, has not been brought on record.

Rather the purchaser has been shown as the power of attorney of the seller-petitioner and the writ petition is supported by affidavit of Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel, power of attorney holder of Amraji Ataji,
the petitioner.

Apart from the description of the petitioner in the array of parties and reference in the affidavit about the power of attorney, there is absolutely no whisper in the writ petition about the alleged power of attorney.

sentences.text: It is sought to be submitted by Mr. A.M.Parekh, the learned NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026

undefined advocate appearing for the original petitioner/appellant herein that the writ petition and the present appeal, cannot be said to have been filed by Amraji Ataji in his personal capacity, inasmuch as, he has represented himself through the power of attorney holder namely Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel, who is now the owner of the land-in-question by virtue of the sale deed dated 29.12.2023.

However, this factual statement made at the Bar, cannot be appreciated for the simple reason that there is no disclosure in the writ petition itself about the sale deed or the power of attorney given to Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel by Amraji Ataji.

The challenge to the order dated 14.08.2025 passed under the directions issued by this Court in the judgment and order dated 27.03.2025 in the previous writ petition filed by Amraji Ataji,
cannot be entertained as the person who has approached this Court on both the occassions namely Amraji Ataji has left with no right, title or interest in the land-in-question.
9. Both the writ petitions
having
been filed by the same person, namely Amraji Ataji without disclosing the factum of the execution of the sale deed, are nothing but sheer abuse of process of this Court.

10. Besides that, it is also pertinent to note that Mr. Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel in whose favour the sale deed 29.12.2023 has been executed transferring the land-in-question, had filed a Review Application, namely Misc. Civil Application (for review) No. 2261 of 2025 in another writ petition namely Special Civil Application No. 1956 of 2009 filed by the brother of the original petitioner herein, namely Maganji Ataji Baria, seeking for recall/review of the judgment and order dated 19.08.2025.

By the NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined said decision, the writ petition has been disposed of granting the liberty to the petitioner therein to make his representation with respect to the allotment of final plot or compensation in lieu of 960 sq. mtrs. of Revenue Survey No. 87/1, which has been reserved for the public purpose in the T.P. Scheme No. 243.

By the order dated 12.12.2025 passed by this Court in the Review Application noticing that in Village Form No.6 entry of the sale deed dated 29.12.2023 in favour of the applicant Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel had been made and that the judgment and order dated 19.08.2025 of disposal of the writ petition filed by Maganji Ataji Baria had been obtained behind the back of the actual owner, the order of disposal of the said writ petition has been recalled.

It would not be out of place to mention here that even the Review Application seeking recall of the judgment and order dated 19.08.2025 had been filed through the same advocate Mr. A.M.Parekh by the review applicant namely Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel, who is the deponent in the writ petition out of which the present appeal has arisen.

11. Besides that, a Special Civil Application No. 18862 of 2023 has been filed by one Ghanshyambhai Kantibhai Patel, appears to be the brother of Hasmukhbhai Kantibhai Patel, with respect to the same issue even before the execution of the sale deed dated 29.12.2023.
In the said writ petition, the petitioner therein was also represented by the same learned advocate, namely Mr. A.M.Parekh.

From the order dated 03.11.2023 of the issuance of the notice in the said writ petition filed by Ghanshyambhai Kantibhai Patel, it may be noted that an undertaking was given by the petitioner therein that no further construction would be put up.

sentences.text:
From the above noted facts, it is more than evident that four NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined different persons filed four writ petitions and the review application at different points of time while acting in concert, only with a view to retain the illegal possession of the land-in-question, namely the Revenue Survey No. 87/1,
area 960 sq.mtrs., which has been reserved for the public purposes in the T.P.Scheme No. 243.
13.

Considering the manner in which the matter has been proceeded by Amraji Ataji, the original petitioner/appellant herein, just in order to retain the physical possession of the land-in-question without there being any right, title or interest in the land left with him with the execution of the sale deed, and for the fact that the factum of transfer of title to the third party has not been disclosed in the writ petition out of which the present proceeding has arisen, we are of the considered view that filing of the present appeal and the writ petition at the instance of Amraji Ataji is nothing but a sheer abuse of the process of the Court.

14. For the deliberate concealment on the part of the petitioner namely Amraji Ataji in two rounds of litigation brought before this Court, even after parting away with his right, title or interest in the land-in-question, we find it fit and proper to dismiss the present appeal affirming the order passed by the learned single Judge, with the cost of Rs. 1,00,000/-, which shall be deposited before the Registrar General of the High Court within a period of three weeks from today, failing which the proceedings for recovery of the cost amount as arrears of land revenue shall be initiated against the original petitioner/appellant herein namely Amraji Ataji.

Apart from that, we also direct the Registrar General of the High Court to initiate the proceedings for perjury against the petitioner namely Amraji Ataji who has repeatedly filed writ petitions by making false NEUTRAL CITATION C/LPA/1160/2025 ORDER DATED: 05/02/2026 undefined statements before the Court of law.
15. With the dismissal of the Letters Patent Appeal, the pending Civil Application for stay stands disposed of.
